title: Deployment Baton — Weekly Checklist & Rollout Journal (Feb 2027) [Draft]
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working weekly deployment baton — a compact checklist + live journal for small-to-medium rollouts (hosted API patches, minor serving-runtime tweaks, and Dedicated config flips). Goal: give one on-call deployment owner a single sheet to run a 3-hour window with clear signal checks, escalation steps, and a short release notes stub to hand off to growth/CS after stabilization.

Context / when to use:
- Use for fast cadence releases where we expect incremental traffic shifts (0 -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) over ~3 hours.
- Not for major model swaps, DB migrations, or infra re-architects (those follow the full launch binder).
- Assumes QA smoke passed on staging, telemetry capture enabled, and preflight traffic-sim run within 48h.

Roles (single-line):
- Deployment Baton (owner): coordinates, flips routes, runs checks — typically release-engineering.
- SRE/Telemetry lead: watches latency/error budgets, owns circuit breakers.
- Dev owner: can patch/rollback the change and debug.
- EM/Product comms: prepares release note snippet and customer-facing status if needed.

Pre-flight (24–72h before):
- Confirm canary config present in console and env flags match deploy PR (PR link above).
- Sanity run: smoke tests (end-to-end generation, KV-cache hit checks) on staging — paste outputs to this doc.
- Telemetry hooks: ensure metrics pipeline has a fresh job and traces are sampled (JIRA-OBS-2891).
- Runload sim: short ramp test for 5m at expected QPS; check downstream latencies and token-serving percentiles.
- Prepare rollback PR(s) or patch branch and validate rollback path locally.
- Update comms channel: #deployments and announce tentative window (add to shift calendar).

Day-of quick checklist (owner reads aloud at T-90m):
- T-90m: thumbs-up from SRE & dev owner in Slack.
- T-60m: ensure infra capacity (GPU nodes count, Dedicated pools) — check dedicated-dashboard and capacity-alerts.
- T-45m: snapshot current canary/production traffic split & token-cost baseline (console -> per-route cost).
- T-30m: confirm monitoring runbooks are open and visible (PagerDuty escalation ready).
- T-15m: sanity endpoint ping and function/tool calling smoke (3 example flows).

Rollout ladder (typical, adjustable):
- Step 0: Deploy artifact to canary fleet (0% user traffic). Verify service-level health + readiness. (owner action: deploy + post-deploy smoke)
- Step 1: Flip to 2% traffic for 10m — run signal checklist below.
- Step 2: 5% for 20m if green.
- Step 3: 25% for 30m (or until stabilization window).
- Step 4: 75% for 30m — monitor saturated paths.
- Step 5: 100% and tidy the canary, update route tags.

Signal checklist (at each step):
- Error rate (5m, 1m): increase > 2x baseline? pause/rollback.
- p95 latency for text/generation endpoints: increase > +30% absolute or >250ms absolute over baseline => investigate.
- Token cost per request: sudden spike? investigate model variant mismatch.
- Service-specific alarms: high queue depth, KV cache miss rate spike, CUDA memory pressure.
- User-facing anomalies: customer Slack pings, status page incidents.
- Quality check: sample 20 inferences; check for hallucination regressions in targeted prompt sets.

Automatic safety gates (config):
- If 1m error rate > 1% absolute and >2x baseline — auto throttle to previous stable split.
- If p99 latency > SLA by 2x for 5m — trigger immediate rollback.
- If SRE manually declares incident in PD channel — abort and follow incident runbook.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- Owner posts to #deployments with "rollback now" + reason tag.
- Flip traffic to last stable variant (console rollback button or route toggle) and confirm -5% to +0% within 2m.
- Open hotfix PR if root cause known; otherwise keep route at previous stable and call triage.
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24h.

Communication script (owner):
- At start: "Starting deployment baton for REL-4123; expected ~3h window. I will post step updates at each ladder step. SRE on watch: @sre_oncall."
- On pause/rollback: short summary + primary symptom + immediate mitigation.
- On finish: stable timestamp + short release-note draft for product/CS.

Release notes stub (fill after stable):
- Title: minor runtime tweak and canary model pin — REL-4123
- Summary (1 line): Short latency-optimized kernel selection rollout for text-gen routes; no API changes.
- Impact: expected lower p95 on long-seq requests; no customer-facing interface changes.
- Rollout: gradual canary -> full in ~3h (completed at TIMESTAMP).
- Notes for customers: none; internal teams (SRE/CS) notified.

Weekly calendar sketch (this doc is the baton template):
- Monday: preflight smoke & telemetry checks (owner: dev oncall).
- Wednesday: small-batch rollouts (owner rotates weekly).
- Friday afternoon: freeze for larger migrations.
- Follow-up: 48h stability check and cost-sample capture (token-cost comparisons).

Loose issues / TODOs (we're iterating):
- Add one-click rollback widget to console that also captures a snapshot for forensics (Rina to prototyp e).
- Automate the 20-sample quality check and store diffs in an artifacts bucket (Samir owns).
- Integrate quick links to the most-recent canary logs in the baton view.

Notes & freeform observations from last run (2027-02-03):
- Observed: KV cache miss spikes at 25% step, correlated with a new sidecar release (tracked in PR 2387). Solved by pinning sidecar revision on canary.
- Tip: run a short synthetic workload that mirrors top-10 user prompts — this caught a regression that metrics alone did not.
- Consider: default ladder with a 15m hold at 5% for more conservative customers.

Appendix: quick Slack snippets (copy/paste)
- Start: "[DEPLOY-BATON] Starting REL-4123 — owner @Asha; SRE watching @sre_oncall; will post step updates"
- Pause: "[DEPLOY-BATON] Pausing at 5% — spike in token-cost and p95 latency; investigating (see JIRA-OBS-2891)"
- Rollback: "[DEPLOY-BATON] Rolling back REL-4123 to variant v1.4.7 — reason: p99 latency breach"

End of doc — owner: Asha Patel. Keep this file as the live journal during the window; paste post-deployment notes above the issues section and flag any followups for triage.
